claim.summary: For every prime p, over the compact base Q_{n,p} (n=2^l, l>=2, m=n+1 rows of l bits, v=(n+1)l) with accuracy h=3(p-1)l and complete one-level ENS blocks affine in the old bits: if the proper high blocks ((p-1)r>h(k+1)) are M coordinate blocks (input spans spanned by literals x_b-c_b, c_b in F_p) and either M<=k or, with r=3l(k+1)+1 and V=pv (V=v under consistent pins), M prod_{i<t}(1-(r-l i)/V)<=k-t for some 0<=t<=k-1, there is no ordinary-PC refutation through any D>=1 with 2k(D+1)-1<=n. So M such blocks are excluded through floor((n+1)/(2M))-1 when that is >=1, i.e. M<=(n+1)/4. Proof: a product of pinned literal factors in distinct rows (one per block, or the greedy choice over F_p literals) is a nonzero f in L_k with zero restriction to every high flat; the rest of the all-prime affine exclusion proof (literal cofactors, p-1 coefficient rows, weighted ceilings, signed row separation) is unchanged.
claim.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer with corrections (D>=2h+1 found unused and dropped, F_p greedy argument written out, ledger and choice paragraph).

claim.summary: Over F2 in Braun's finite-parameter setting (m>0, l>=2, n=2^l, h=3l, complete old-affine family adjoined to Q_{m,l}), if the proper blocks of rank >h(k+1) are M coordinate blocks (input spans spanned by literals x_b+c_b) and either M<=k or, with r=h(k+1)+1 and V=2v (V=v under consistent pins), M prod_{i<t}(1-(r-l i)/V)<=k-t for some 0<=t<=k-1, there is no ordinary-PC refutation through any D>=2h+1 with 2k(D+1)-1<=n. So M such blocks are excluded through D=floor((n+1)/(2M))-1 when that is >=2h+1. For M<=k spread coordinate blocks of r bits in distinct rows with ln M>=-(kr/m)ln(1-1/l), the exact summed restriction ranks on L_k are >= dim L_k. Proof: fix one pinned bit per block in fresh rows (weight prod(x_b+c_b) in L_k with zero restriction); Braun's restriction-ideal lemma, weighted removal and row separation finish; Jensen for the spread bound. The saving is a cover by single literals.

claim.summary: In Braun's F2 setting, for M proper coordinate blocks each pinning at least r>l(k-1) bits, k>=1, with V=v under consistent pins and V=2v otherwise: if M prod_{i<t}(1-(r-l i)/V) <= k-t for some integer 0<=t<=k-1, a nonzero product of at most k affine forms x_b+c in distinct rows lies in L_k and has zero ordinary restriction to every flat. At t=0: any M<=k such blocks have a common kernel. Proof: t greedy literal choices by double counting, then one literal per remaining block in a fresh row. At l=16, D=107 (k=303, r=14593) it certifies ln M up to 7.14 (consistent pins) and 6.00 (general), against the summed count's 4.25 and the Harris certificate's 5.44.
